title: Sort machined blocks with a go/no-go gap gauge
instruction: Check each of the seven aluminium blocks with the gauge: set it on the green GO gap and, only if it drops in, then set it on the red NO-GO gap. A block that drops into GO but not into NO-GO is in tolerance: put it in the green tray. Put every other block in the red tray.
context: Checking parts against fixed-limit gauges is routine work for machinists and quality inspectors, and passing an out-of-tolerance block (an escape) is the costly mistake. Unlike picking the one pin that fits a hole, every block in a batch must be classified against two limits.
setup: Station table. Coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y = +0.305 (left) and y = -0.305 (right). Loose: seven bare aluminium blocks, each 50 mm long (along x) by 20 mm tall, lying flat; their widths (along y): block 1 30.5 mm, 2 34.5, 3 28.5, 4 25.5, 5 35.0, 6 29.5, 7 25.0; specified width 30.0 +- 3.0 mm. Each weighs 2.7 g per mm of width (68 to 95 g). Their numbers are written on their undersides, out of the cameras' view. Seven start places: four at y = +0.30, x 0.16, 0.25, 0.34, 0.43, and three at y = -0.30, x 0.16, 0.25, 0.34. Which block goes in which place is shuffled by a layout number: the README lists layouts 0 to 9 and the rule for any number. The screenshot and the submitted runs use layout 3: blocks 7, 1, 3, 4 at y = +0.30 and 6, 5, 2 at y = -0.30, nearest first. Fixed, screwed down: the gauge, centred at (0.13, 0): a dark grey steel base 100 x 160 x 10 mm (x, y, z) with two pairs of anvils on top, each anvil 10 x 20 x 15 mm. The green pair forms the GO gap, 33.0 mm between inner faces, centred at y = +0.04; the red pair forms the NO-GO gap, 27.0 mm, centred at y = -0.04. Both gaps run along x, so a block lying along x drops into a gap when it is narrower, onto the base 15 mm below the anvil tops. Two open trays across the midline, each 80 x 220 mm inside, 5 mm floor, 6 mm walls standing 25 mm above the table: the red reject tray centred at x 0.24 and the green pass tray centred at x 0.35. Real-world build: blocks are 6061 bar stock milled to width (+-0.05 mm) and numbered underneath; the gauge base, anvils and trays are printed PLA or machined aluminium, the anvils set to the gap widths with a caliper, screwed or glued down. A camera records the gauge from above for the whole trial.
scoring: Blocks 1, 3 and 6 are in tolerance; 2, 4, 5 and 7 are not. A gauge check of a block at a gap is valid when, for at least 0.3 s, it lies seated in the gap (flat on the gauge base between that gap's anvils) or rests on that gap's anvil tops, flat or wedged between them, without reaching the base and with the gripper not holding it. A narrow block held up on top of a gap is no check. Each block needs a valid GO check; a block seated in GO then needs a valid NO-GO check after it; one that stays out of GO needs none. A block is in a tray when its whole footprint is inside the tray's walls, its bottom rests on the tray floor or on a block in the tray, and it is still (under 1 cm/s); held above the floor, on a rim or anywhere else counts for nothing. C counts blocks with valid checks, in that order, that end in the right tray. F counts in-tolerance blocks in the red tray (false rejects) and E out-of-tolerance blocks in the green tray (escapes), checked or not. Score = (C - 2F - 2E) / 7, at least 0; if E is 1 or more, at most 0.25. Read the end state after the arms stop and open, with a top photo and a tape. Real trial: the checks are judged from the overhead video, or a photo of each block seated in or resting across each gap with the gripper open and clear. Full score (1.0) is all seven blocks checked and in the right trays; the trial ends early once that holds for 1 s. Sorting correctly without the checks scores 0; every block in one tray scores 0; checking every block and then sorting at random scores about 0.052 on average.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Set the next trial's layout: place each block, by the number on its underside, in that layout's start place, lying along x. Start a new video for the trial's checks.
fidelity: Approximate. Blocks, gauge and trays are rigid boxes with one shared rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The tolerance is scaled up: each block clears or misses each gap by at least 1.5 mm in width, so the simulated contacts resolve it; real gauges work to hundredths of a millimetre. Anvils have square edges with no chamfer. Checks are read from the block poses at every step, where a real trial reads them from video.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (layout 3, all 6,000 steps); demo: 1.0 (layout 3, 3,971 steps)
